key_insight: RLVR gets no relative-advantage learning signal when a prompt’s sampled answers all pass or all fail. FADE proposes separating policy ability from prompt difficulty to better target prompts that produce informative, mixed outcomes.
problem_solved: Generation budget is wasted on uninformative prompt groups, while per-prompt pass-rate trackers conflate changing policy competence with prompt difficulty.
method: Factor prompt success into policy ability across reasoning skills and prompt difficulty, rather than tracking only a combined pass rate.
Use this factored view for online scheduling that targets prompts likely to yield both passing and failing completions.
impact: More informative prompt selection could improve RLVR’s learning efficiency per generated completion. The supplied abstract is truncated, so implementation details and measured gains cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Three outcome groups: all-pass, all-fail, and mixed—with only mixed outcomes highlighted as informative.
Factor diagram separating policy skill ability from prompt difficulty.
Scheduling loop: select prompts → generate completions → verify rewards → update policy and scheduler.
Conceptual ability-versus-difficulty heatmap highlighting the informative frontier.
paper_title: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
paper_authors: Tomas Duncun, Jonah Ellison, Mateo Ruiz, Hanae Fujita, Ingrid Solberg
